# arunodhayan's fine-tuning driver — vendored verbatim, not ours

`train.py` (1138 lines) is the *actual* script that produced the fine-tuned checkpoints and
zero-shot reference scores referenced in `docs/checkpoints.md` and `experiment_summary.md`
Phase 3, item 12 (the full arunodhayan highpass+skeleton-recall+affinity fine-tune, which
regressed every metric substantially). It is vendored here **unmodified**, exactly as it ran,
because this is what actually happened — not a reconstruction of what should have happened.

**This is not our code.** It's arunodhayan's own training driver (his 3rd-place solution),
adapted by hand for this fine-tuning attempt. See `docs/attribution.md` for the full source
citation.

## What it actually is, plainly

- A single, monolithic, notebook-derived script: `os.environ["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = "0,1"`
  set at import time, several absolute/dataset-name-baked-in paths
  (`19feb_vesuvius-surface-nnunet-preprocessed_prob0.8`, `19feb_nnUNet_data_...`), and a bare
  `full_pipeline(epochs=8000)` call at the very bottom of the file — running the script *is*
  the invocation, there's no CLI or `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard.
- `finetune_cascade.yaml.orig` sat in the same directory during the real run but **was never
  read by `train.py`** — the association between the two files is historical (they lived side
  by side), not functional. Don't assume the yaml's settings describe what actually happened;
  the hardcoded values inside `train.py` itself are the only real record.
- Do not edit this file. If you want a readable, config-driven starting point for a *future*
  fine-tune run, see `src/vesuvius_surface/training/finetune/arunodhayan_cascade_driver.py` —
  a clean rewrite extracted from reading this script's logic, explicitly **not** verified to
  reproduce this script's exact output bit-for-bit. See `docs/reproducibility_notes.md` for
  the full, honest gap this represents.
